interactions.note: Additive bleeding risk — concurrent use needs INR monitoring; avoid unless specifically directed.
NSAID may reduce aspirin's antiplatelet effect and raises GI bleeding risk.
Antibiotic may potentiate warfarin — monitor INR.
Fluoroquinolone increases INR — significant bleeding risk.
Omeprazole inhibits clopidogrel activation — consider pantoprazole instead.
Iron chelates fluoroquinolones — separate doses by 2 hours.
Calcium binds levothyroxine — separate doses by 4 hours.
Additive hypoglycemia risk — counsel patient on warning signs.
Dual NSAID exposure — GI bleeding and renal risk.
Additive hypotension/hydration effect — check BP and electrolytes.
